met_analysis:
The Deep Depression over Western parts of central Chhattisgarh and adjoining east Madhya Pradesh moved southwestwards with a speed of 12 kmph during past 6 hours, and lies centered at 0830 hrs IST of today, the 30th July 2026, over westcentral Chhattisgarh and adjoining areas of Vidarbha & southeast Madhya Pradesh near latitude 21.0°N and longitude 81.3°E, close to south of Durg (Chhattisgarh), 30 km east-southeast of Rajnandgaon (Chhattisgarh), 50 km west-southwest of Raipur (Chhattisgarh), 130 km east-southeast of Gondia (Maharashtra) and 160 km east-northeast of Bramhapuri (Maharashtra). It is very likely to move nearly westwards across Chhattisgarh and weaken gradually into a depression during next 12 hours. Thereafter, it is likely to move west-northwestwards across Vidarbha & adjoining south Madhya Pradesh as a depression during subsequent 24 hours.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Jaisalmer, Raisen, centre of Deep Depression over Western parts of westcentral Chhattisgarh and adjoining areas of Vidarbha & southeast Madhya Pradesh, Gopalpur thence southeastwards towards Central parts of Bay of Bengal and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The east-west shear zone roughly along latitude 21°N across central & adjoining north peninsular India between 3.1 & 7.6 km above mean sea level tilting southwards with height persists.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over Punjab & neighbourhood now lies over north Haryana & neighbourhood between 3.1 & 5.8 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over central Assam at 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
A offshore trough at mean sea level runs from South Gujarat to North Kerala.
